transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Head of ML, Sapphire Analytics), Leah Kim (CTO), Marcus Voss (Infra Lead)
---
Auto-summary: quick discovery re: model selection; customer has multilingual production assistant that needs long context and tools to call internal inventory and compliance APIs. Interested in Dedicated for production but wants to validate Hosted for POC.
---
00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros, i'm alex with redwood, priya is our se, and we'll run through current stack and model needs.
00:07 Jamal Ortiz: hey thanks, jamal here, head of ml, we run a customer support assistant and an insights pipeline, lots of multi-lingual queries.
00:12 Leah Kim: leah, cto; mainly interested in compliance and infra impact.
00:16 Alex Chen: great; high level — you're evaluating open models and want to understand hosted vs dedicated vs private?
00:22 Jamal Ortiz: yes. two big constraints: long context, we often need 50k to 100k tokens for multi-turn threads and docs; and multilingual — spanish, french, korean, japanese — quality must be near parity. Also tool-calling: our assistant needs to call internal APIs to fetch invoices and to launch workflows.
00:40 Priya Nair: ok interesting, for context length we're seeing two patterns; either use a model variant with native long context (32k/100k) or use chunking + KV cache. our runtime supports kv cache and prefix caching but sometimes prefetched k-v cache gets transcribed in docs as "K-V cash" etc, but functionally it helps reduce recomputation.
00:58 Marcus Voss: are there size limits on hosted? like can we use 100k on hosted redwood?
01:02 Alex Chen: hosted supports model variants with long context depending on the model — e.g., some open models we've validated at 32k and certain ones at 100k, but availability and latency differ. For guaranteed throughput and predictable latency you'd look at Dedicated where you reserve GPU pools. For on-prem/private we can ship a private control plane, VPC connectors and HSM/KMS integration for keys.
01:22 Jamal Ortiz: what's the quality delta between models — we're comparing mosaic, llama-like open models, and some newer community forks. Also, cost for 100k contexts seems scary.
01:30 Priya Nair: totally. we've done a model matrix — generally as context grows cost grows linearly with tokens but choices like quantization and batching reduce cost. open models differ: some have better multilingual pretraining — e.g., certain Llama-variants perform ok on european languages but maybe worse on asian languages. Anthropic and OpenAI still lead on certain instruction-following benchmarks, but customers choose open models for cost and control. we'll share a model comparison sheet.
01:54 Leah Kim: on security, we need SOC2, SSO, SAML, and encryption keys managed in our KMS. can you do bring-your-own-key and HSM?
02:02 Alex Chen: yes, Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM, audit logs, RBAC and SSO integrations. Dedicated also supports private networking and dedicated pools with extra isolation. Hosted has tenant isolation and SOC2, but if you need full VPC egress control we recommend Private.
02:20 Jamal Ortiz: for the POC i think we want to start hosted if possible to move fast, but the production bar will likely be Dedicated or Private because of PII. is there an easy migration path?
02:29 Priya Nair: yes, the API and config are consistent across modes — same endpoints and model names, you can pin versions. in practice customers start on Hosted and then replicate config to Dedicated/Private; we help with model pinning and rollouts.
02:40 Marcus Voss: what about tool-calling? we need the model to call internal APIs securely, and to restrict which functions it can call. can you do function-level RBAC or allowlisted endpoints?
02:50 Priya Nair: we support function/tool calling and structured outputs. you can control which external tools are exposed, and you can run a proxy in your VPC to mediate calls. for Hosted we offer secure connectors; for Private you manage the network egress. mention that sometimes transcriptions show it as "function plug calling" which is the same idea.
03:06 Jamal Ortiz: we also care about multilingual tokenization — some of our tokenizers produce different token counts for asian languages, making cost unpredictable. any guidance?
03:14 Priya Nair: yea, tokenization varies. we recommend benchmarking with representative queries in each language and we can run a tokenization/cost estimate. also some models have better tokenizer coverage for certain scripts. we'll include per-language model guidance in the comparison.
03:30 Leah Kim: latency — our SLA target is 200-400ms p95 for chat flows; is that realistic with long contexts?
03:36 Alex Chen: for short contexts and smaller models sure; for 32k+ contexts latency increases. we mitigate with KV caching, early truncation, and reranking strategies. Dedicated with reserved GPUs and tuned kernels can hit lower variance and better p95 compared to shared Hosted.
03:55 Jamal Ortiz: and concurrency? we expect spikes around product launches, like 200 concurrent requests peak. how does autoscaling work?
04:02 Priya Nair: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity; you set your pool sizes and policies. Hosted autoscaling is automatic but subject to region capacity; for spikes the routing layer can fall back to compatible variants. we'll show a throughput vs cost tradeoff later.
04:20 Marcus Voss: compliance — do you keep logs? retention policies? can we have zero retention for request payloads?
04:27 Alex Chen: yes, you control retention. Private gives you full control; Dedicated can be configured with stricter retention and audit logs. Hosted has configurable retention windows and we can offer per-account policies. we'll share the security doc.
04:40 Jamal Ortiz: ok sounds good. anything about model hallucinations and safety? we need guardrails for invoices and financial data.
04:47 Priya Nair: we recommend output validation, tool-based retrieval for factual docs, reranker and eval hooks in console. Redwood Optimize can detect regressions across eval sets. also function-calling with structured outputs helps reduce hallucination when retrieving data.
05:05 Alex Chen: recap: we'll send model comparison + pricing, security pack, and run a benchmark on 8k and 32k contexts with your sample data. priya will run the bench and alex will send pricing. schedule technical deep dive for next week.
05:18 Leah Kim: thanks, we'll also provide sample payloads and expected concurrency numbers.
05:22 Jamal Ortiz: timeline — POC in 2-3 weeks, then decision for Dedicated or Private in 6-8 weeks depending on results.
05:29 Alex Chen: perfect. i'll follow up in the crm with next steps.
05:33 [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: several product terms were slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "function plug" for function calling). there was some crosstalk during the throughput section.
